title: Expanded Attributes and Appositions
summary: Building and unpacking dense noun phrases with participial attributes, complements, and appositions.
whyItMatters: Academic and journalistic German often compresses whole clauses into noun phrases; recognizing their internal structure makes difficult texts manageable.

mentalModel.title: Find the noun phrase frame
mentalModel.content: Locate the article or determiner, the ending-bearing attribute, and the head noun before interpreting embedded details.

mentalModel.title: Expand to understand, compress to write
mentalModel.content: Turn a dense attribute into a relative clause, then decide which version best serves clarity and register.

ruleBlocks.title: Extend participial attributes
ruleBlocks.content: Participles can carry objects, adverbs, prepositional phrases, and negation before the head noun.

ruleBlocks.title: Keep adjective endings visible
ruleBlocks.content: The final participle or adjective receives the ending determined by article, case, gender, and number.

ruleBlocks.title: Use appositions for identification
ruleBlocks.content: Set explanatory noun phrases in matching case, usually separated by commas.

examples.de: Die erst Jahrzehnte später öffentlich diskutierten Ereignisse prägen die Debatte bis heute.
examples.en: The events discussed publicly only decades later continue to shape the debate.

examples.de: Der von mehreren Forschenden unabhängig bestätigte Befund gilt als belastbar.
examples.en: The finding independently confirmed by several researchers is considered robust.

examples.de: Mit Lea Baumann, der Leiterin des Archivs, wurde ein neues Projekt entwickelt.
examples.en: A new project was developed with Lea Baumann, the head of the archive.

commonMistakes.wrong: Give the participle no adjective ending.
commonMistakes.correct: Decline it like an adjective inside the noun phrase.
commonMistakes.reason: Its participial origin does not remove agreement.

commonMistakes.wrong: Compress so much that the head noun becomes hard to find.
commonMistakes.correct: Use a relative clause when readability suffers.
commonMistakes.reason: Formal density is useful only while structure remains clear.

comparisons.summary: Historical texts provide authentic dense descriptions of events, actors, and sources.
Source presentations use attributes and appositions to identify provenance and relevance concisely.
